title: Boyle's Law and Inverse Proportionality of Gas Volume and Pressure
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Boyle's Law states that the volume V of a gas at constant temperature is inversely proportional to its pressure P. If P = 14.7 lb/in^2 when V = 1000 in^3, what is the volume V when P = 23.4 lb/in^2?

steps.title: State Boyle's Law as an Inverse Variation Equation
steps.explanation: Because V and P are inversely proportional at constant temperature, their product PV equals a constant k.
steps.why: Inverse proportionality between V and P implies PV = k is constant during isothermal compression.

steps.title: Calculate the Constant k
steps.explanation: Substitute P = 14.7 lb/in^2 and V = 1000 in^3 into k = PV to find k = 14,700.
steps.why: The initial state (P_1, V_1) fixes the isothermal constant k = P_1 V_1.

steps.title: Compute V When P = 23.4 lb/in^2
steps.explanation: Divide k = 14,700 by P = 23.4 to obtain V = 24,500 / 39 in^3, or approximately 628.21 in^3.
steps.why: Increasing the pressure from 14.7 to 23.4 lb/in^2 compresses the gas volume proportionally.
